results.text:
Figure O.1
Title: "Income per capita of middle-income countries relative to that of the United States has been stagnant for decades." 

Chart type: multi-series line chart.

X-axis: years 1970 to 2022.
Y-axis: "Share of US GNI per capita (%)" with tick marks from 0 to 60 in increments of 5.

Legend/series:
- Dark line: "Middle-income countries"
- Orange line: "Middle-income countries, excluding China"
- Light gray comparison lines labeled in the plot: "Korea, Rep.", "Poland", and "Chile"

Visible relationships/trends:
- The two aggregate middle-income-country series stay low relative to the United States, generally around the low single digits to about 8% over the period, with a modest rise after roughly 2008 and a slight easing after the mid-2010s.
- The "excluding China" series tracks slightly below the full middle-income-country series for most of the period.
- Korea, Rep. rises strongly from the mid-teens in the 1970s to just above 50% in the late 2010s/early 2020s, then remains near that level.
- Poland rises from around 10% in 1970 to the mid-20% range by 2022.
- Chile rises from roughly the low-to-mid teens in the late 1970s/1980s to about 20%+ by 2022.

Source: WDR 2024 team using data from WDI (World Development Indicators) (Data Catalog), World Bank, Washington, DC, https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037712.

Note: The plotted lines indicate the trend of average income per capita in middle-income countries and in middle-income countries, excluding China, relative to income per capita of the United States (considered the economic frontier country). Country definitions are based on the first World Development Report (World Bank 1978), in which low-income countries have gross national income (GNI) per capita of US$250 or less; middle-income countries have GNI per capita of more than US$250; and industrialized (high-income) countries consist of member countries of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, except for Greece, Portugal, Spain, and Türkiye, which are classified as middle-income countries.
